title: Add masked plaintext export support
description: * This change adds address masking capabilities to the Qt Export Dissection dialog (`export_dissection_dialog.cpp`) and the plaintext print engine (`epan/print.c`).

notes.body:
added 8 commits
  • fbb92907...eecf92eb - 6 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • e1a0c4af - Qt: Add native address sanitization to plain text export
  • fc04ab52 - Fix build errors by adding missing errno.h headers
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/26235/diffs?diff_id=1973154622&start_sha=fbb929077a12398e5d13d47b17b002237e2ceb9e)

> It also includes missing `<errno.h>` header inclusions across several files to fix build compilation errors.

Please show examples of those build errors. I've done several builds on macOS of the main branch and have not seen any errors due to missing errno.h includes.

Could the masked plaintext export mechanisms be moved to the epan/print.c code, or even to the epan/proto.c code, so that it doesn't use regex hacks to recognize IPv4 and MAC addresses, but can recognize the data types of named fields, which may also allow it to be more easily extended to _other_ data types, e.g. IPv6 addresses?

I encountered error: ‘errno’ undeclared during local compilation on Linux when building without certain precompiled headers. I can split or revert the \<errno.h\> changes if they aren't needed for macOS/upstream standard builds."

Thanks for the feedback, Guy. That makes complete sense—using epan/print.c to check field types directly (like FT_IPv4 or FT_ETHER) is much cleaner than using regex in the Qt dialog. I'll refactor the logic into epan.

added 1 commit
  • 0b2de7dd - epan: Refactor address masking engine to use field types
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/26235/diffs?diff_id=1973298755&start_sha=fc04ab5223a33a3683b0ebcfb928b007f5cffa8b)

> I encountered error: ‘errno’ undeclared during local compilation on Linux when building without certain precompiled headers.

I'm not seeing that when doing a standard build on Ubuntu 22.04. Those problems might be an issue with your build setup.

> I can split or revert the \<errno.h\> changes if they aren't needed for macOS/upstream standard builds.

They don't appear to be necessary for standard builds, so please revert them.

Hi @guyharris,

I've refactored the address masking implementation according to your feedback:

* **Engine Refactor:** Moved address sanitization directly into `epan/print.c` (`proto_tree_print_node()`).
* **Field-Type Checking:** Masking now evaluates `fi->hfinfo->type` directly (`FT_IPv4`, `FT_IPv6`, and `FT_ETHER`) rather than running regex transformations on the rendered text in the Qt UI.
* **UI Cleanup:** Removed the regular expression handling from `export_dissection_dialog.cpp` and exposed `mask_addresses` via `print_args_t` in `file.h`.

Please let me know if you'd like any further adjustments to the field-type logic or if you'd prefer I separate the `<errno.h>` build fixes into a standalone PR. Thanks!

Done! I've reverted all unnecessary `<errno.h>` header inclusions across the repository.

The MR is now clean and focused purely on the address masking refactor in `epan/print.c`. Thanks!
